note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in NV.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: Pyramid Lake Road
byways.designation: Nevada Scenic Byway; part of the Pyramid Lake National Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 445 along the west shore of Pyramid Lake, reservation boundary south of Sutcliffe to Warrior Point, Washoe County

facts.fact: The scenic section is the 12.5 miles of SR 445 inside the Pyramid Lake Indian Reservation, running along the west shore through Sutcliffe to Warrior Point.
Pyramid Lake is the biggest remnant of ancient Lake Lahontan, and the lake's colour shifts between blue and gray with the sky.
Visitors need a Pyramid Lake Paiute Tribe permit, sold online or at the ranger station in Sutcliffe.
The lake takes its name from a tufa formation.

byways.review: Catalog line 2457 is the whole national byway (SR 445, SR 446 and SR 447 segments); the three state byways all point to it.

byways.name: Mt Rose Highway
byways.where: SR 431 between SR 28 at Incline Village and Reno, Washoe County

facts.fact: SR 431 climbs the Carson Range from Incline Village to Mount Rose Summit, 8,911 ft, which NDOT has called the highest year-round pass in the Sierra Nevada.
A view area on the western ascent has markers pointing out Sierra peaks around Lake Tahoe, and both approaches to the summit have hairpin curves.
On the east side the road passes the Mount Rose ski area and overlooks of Reno and Washoe Valley.

byways.review: No agency page found for this byway; url left null.

byways.name: Lake Tahoe North Shore
byways.designation: Nevada Scenic Byway; part of the Lake Tahoe - Eastshore Drive National Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 28 from US 50 at Spooner Junction to the California line at Crystal Bay, Douglas County, Carson City and Washoe County

facts.fact: SR 28 runs 16.3 miles from Spooner Junction on US 50 to the California line at Crystal Bay along the northeast shore of Lake Tahoe; it has been a Nevada scenic byway since June 1994.
Sand Harbor, beside the highway, has beaches among granite boulders, picnic sites under cedars and Jeffrey pines, and the summer Lake Tahoe Shakespeare Festival.
The road passes in and out of Lake Tahoe-Nevada State Park and the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest before reaching Incline Village.

byways.review: Catalog line 2456 covers the national byway (US 50 Stateline to Spooner Junction plus SR 28 to Incline Village). The state byway continues on SR 28 past Incline Village to Crystal Bay, which may be missing from the line.

byways.name: Lamoille Canyon Road
byways.designation: Nevada Scenic Byway; also a National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: Forest Road 660 from SR 227 near Lamoille into Lamoille Canyon, Ruby Mountains, Elko County

facts.fact: Lamoille Canyon, the largest valley in the Ruby Mountains, was carved by glaciers into a U shape with hanging valleys high on Thomas Peak.
The road ends at Road's End trailhead, about 8,800 ft, the northern end of the Ruby Crest National Recreation Trail; near the canyon mouth is the foundation of a 1913 powerhouse that burned in 1971.
The Terraces picnic area sits in a dense aspen stand beside Lamoille Creek, which holds brook and wild rainbow trout.
The Forest Service calls Lamoille Canyon Road a scenic byway and one of the most popular destinations in that part of the state.

byways.review: No standing USFS page for the byway was found (old recarea URL redirects to the forest's recreation index); url left null.

byways.name: Angel Lake Road
byways.where: SR 231 from Wells to Angel Lake, East Humboldt Range, Elko County

facts.fact: SR 231 runs about 11.6 miles from Wells up switchbacks on the east side of the East Humboldt Range to the Angel Lake fee booth, and may close in winter.
Angel Lake is a 13-acre glacial tarn at 8,378 ft under the cliffs of a cirque, named after Warren M. Angel, an early Clover Valley rancher.
The Forest Service describes it as the only alpine lake in the area reached by paved road, with rainbow, brook and tiger trout.

byways.name: US Highways 6/50/93
byways.where: US 6/US 50/US 93 from south of Ely east past Majors Place and over the Snake Range to the Utah line, White Pine County

facts.fact: The 63-mile byway follows US 6/50/93 from south of Ely to the Utah state line near Great Basin National Park; it was designated on March 27, 2000.
This stretch crosses Connors Pass, 7,729 ft, the highest point on US 50 in Nevada, and Sacramento Pass near the ghost town of Osceola.
Ward Charcoal Ovens State Historic Park, a listed attraction of the section, has six beehive ovens used from 1876 to 1879 to process silver ore.

byways.review: No catalog road is this 63-mile segment (the catalog's statewide 'Loneliest Road' line 2033 overlaps it but is not it). No single value in the NDOT route layer selects it; see gis.notes. url null: no agency page found.

byways.name: Lehman Caves Road
byways.where: SR 488 from SR 487 in Baker west to Great Basin National Park, White Pine County

facts.fact: SR 488 runs 5.4 miles from Baker to the main gate of Great Basin National Park, roughly following Lehman Creek; it was designated a scenic byway on March 27, 2000.
The park service routes visitors through Baker and west on Highway 488 for five miles to reach the park.
Great Basin National Park is known for Lehman Caves, ancient bristlecone pines and Wheeler Peak at 13,063 ft.

byways.name: Baker Road
byways.where: SR 487 from the Utah line through Baker to US 6/US 50, White Pine County

facts.fact: SR 487 runs from the Utah line, where it continues Utah State Route 21, northwest through Baker to US 6/US 50, passing pockets of farmland near town.
Baker sits 5 miles east of the main entrance to Great Basin National Park and had a population of 41 in 2020.
The park service warns that Nevada is on Pacific time, so drivers crossing from Utah change clocks.

byways.name: Great Basin Highway
byways.where: US 93 from SR 318 near Crystal Springs via Caliente and Pioche to US 6/US 50 at Majors Place, Lincoln and White Pine counties

facts.fact: The byway is 148.8 miles of US 93 from SR 318 near Crystal Springs to US 6/US 50 at Majors Place, via Caliente and Pioche; it was Nevada's first scenic byway.
The route links five state parks and Great Basin National Park.
Cathedral Gorge State Park, near Panaca, is a narrow valley where erosion has cut spires and cave-like forms in soft bentonite clay.

byways.review: Catalog 2031 'Highway 93' (149 mi) matches the 148.8-mile length. url left null; the NSB Foundation page for US 93 exists but is thin.

byways.name: Mt Charleston Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 157 (Kyle Canyon Road), SR 158 (Deer Creek Road) and SR 156 (Lee Canyon Road), US 95 into the Spring Mountains, Clark County

facts.fact: The byway combines three state routes designated in July 1998: Kyle Canyon Road (SR 157, 13.0 mi), Deer Creek Road (SR 158, 8.8 mi) and Mt. Charleston/Lee Canyon Road (SR 156, 17.5 mi).
The Spring Mountains rise from creosote desert to Charleston Peak at 11,918 ft, with ponderosa pine and white fir on the slopes and bristlecone pine on the high ridges.
The seven Southern Paiute tribes, the Nuwuvi, consider the Spring Mountains the place of creation, and the Spring Mountains Visitor Gateway in Kyle Canyon has a plaza honoring that heritage.

byways.review: NDOT's 2023 map shows the three routes as one byway. The catalog also has kyle-canyon-road-state-route-157-71118 and deer-creek-road-state-route-158-71119, which are parts of this byway (SR 156 has no separate catalog entry).

byways.name: Red Rock Road
byways.where: SR 159 through Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area, from near Blue Diamond to the east boundary of the NCA, Clark County

facts.fact: The byway is 8.8 miles of SR 159 through Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area west of Las Vegas, designated June 30, 1995.
SR 159 runs northwest through the town of Blue Diamond toward Spring Mountain Ranch State Park, then curves northeast around Red Rock Canyon.
Red Rock Canyon's red and cream sandstone cliffs are 17 miles west of the Las Vegas Strip on Charleston Boulevard/SR 159.

byways.review: The state byway is SR 159, not the BLM's 13-mile one-way Scenic Loop (that is the Red Rock Canyon Back Country Byway, catalog 68961). Catalog 2035 is 20 mapped miles against 8.8 designated; check whether its line includes the loop or extra SR 159.

byways.name: Las Vegas Strip All-American Road
byways.designation: All-American Road; Nevada Scenic Byway (South Las Vegas Strip)
byways.where: Las Vegas Boulevard from Russell Road near the Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign to Sahara Avenue, Clark County

facts.fact: The All-American Road is 4.5 miles of Las Vegas Boulevard; FHWA calls it one of the country's only nighttime byways.
The state's South Las Vegas Strip byway runs from Russell Road to Sahara Avenue, designated June 30, 1995; the national designation followed on June 15, 2000.
South of Sahara Avenue the boulevard leaves the City of Las Vegas and becomes the Strip, beginning near the Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign.

byways.review: NDOT's 2023 map draws the north (city) and south (Strip) sections as one 'Las Vegas Strip' entry; the NDOT web page lists the All-American Road and the National Scenic Byway separately, so both are listed here.

byways.name: Las Vegas Boulevard National Scenic Byway
byways.designation: National Scenic Byway; Nevada Scenic Byway (North Las Vegas Strip)
byways.where: Las Vegas Boulevard from Washington Avenue to Sahara Avenue, downtown Las Vegas, Clark County

facts.fact: The national byway is 3.41 miles of Las Vegas Boulevard from the Old Mormon Fort in the north to near the Stratosphere, lined with neon signs for wedding chapels, motels and museums.
Along this stretch are the Old Las Vegas Mormon Fort State Historic Park, the Neon Museum and older motels, bars and wedding chapels from before the megaresorts.
The state designated it on November 28, 2001 as the North Las Vegas Strip; national designation came on October 16, 2009.
NDOT says the byway mixes historic and modern architecture and includes the Neon Museum, which shows signs that once guided travelers of a bygone era.

byways.name: Hoover Dam Road
byways.where: SR 172, Hoover Dam Access Road, from I-11/US 93 near Boulder City east over Rough Summit toward Hoover Dam, Clark County

facts.fact: SR 172 follows the old alignment of US 93 from the I-11 interchange northeast of Boulder City, curving over Rough Summit past the Lakeview viewpoint; the state route ends at the Bureau of Reclamation security checkpoint.
Beyond the checkpoint the access road passes the Mike O'Callaghan-Pat Tillman Memorial Bridge plaza and the visitor center, then crosses the dam into Arizona.
Hoover Dam is a concrete arch-gravity dam in the Black Canyon of the Colorado River, built between 1931 and 1936.

byways.review: Not in the 2015 list; appears on NDOT's 2023 map. The NSB Foundation lists it as 'Hoover Dam Access Road Route 172', 2.8 mi. SR172 in the agency layer stops short of the dam (about 1.4 mi), so the drawn line will end at the checkpoint.

byways.name: Valley of Fire Scenic Byway
byways.where: Valley of Fire Road between the park's west and east entrances, plus White Domes Road, Valley of Fire State Park, Clark County

facts.fact: Valley of Fire State Park holds 40,000 acres of bright red Aztec sandstone, with petrified trees and petroglyphs more than 2,000 years old.
The byway on Valley of Fire Road runs about 10 miles inside the park between the two entrance stations, ending at the east entrance near Elephant Rock; a park entrance fee is charged.
The state's list designates Valley of Fire Road (10.5 mi) and White Domes Road (6.9 mi) on June 30, 1995.

byways.review: NDOT's 2023 map combines the 2015 list's Valley of Fire Road (10.5 mi) and White Domes Road (6.9 mi) into one 'Valley of Fire Scenic Byway'.

byways.name: Bitter Springs Back Country Byway
byways.where: Muddy Mountains, Clark County, near Valley of Fire and Lake Mead

facts.fact: The 28-mile byway passes rock formations of the Muddy Mountains, colourful sandstone and abandoned borax mines; high clearance is required.

byways.name: California Trail Back Country Byway
byways.where: Northeast Elko County, near Thousand Springs

facts.fact: The byway parallels part of the California National Historic Trail, used by more than 250,000 emigrants, and passes wagon ruts and ruined structures near Thousand Springs; it is 96 miles long.

byways.name: Fort Churchill to Wellington Back Country Byway
byways.designation: BLM Back Country Byway (Type I and II)
byways.where: Fort Churchill State Historic Park south to Wellington, Lyon County

facts.fact: The byway runs 67 miles from Fort Churchill, an 1860s Army post built to protect Pony Express riders and settlers, to Wellington; parts need high clearance.
Fort Churchill joined the Nevada State Park system in 1957.

byways.name: Gold Butte Back Country Byway
byways.where: From I-15 exit 112 near Mesquite south into Gold Butte National Monument, Clark County

facts.fact: The 62-mile loop starts at I-15 exit 112 south of Mesquite and Bunkerville and was one of the first designated back country byways.
About 20 miles in is Whitney Pocket, a sandstone wall pitted by wind and water; farther on is Devil's Throat, a 110-foot sinkhole, and the old mining town of Gold Butte, founded in 1908.

byways.name: Lovelock Cave Back Country Byway
byways.designation: BLM Back Country Byway (Type I and II)
byways.where: From Lovelock to Lovelock Cave, Pershing and Churchill counties

facts.fact: Lovelock Cave has yielded 2,000-year-old artifacts including duck decoys and baskets and is known as the cradle of Great Basin archaeology; the byway is 20 miles.
The route crosses what remains of Lake Lahontan.

byways.review: Wording 'is said to have begun' paraphrases BLM's 'cradle of Great Basin archaeology'.

byways.name: Lunar Crater Back Country Byway
byways.where: Loop south of US 6 near mile marker 79, Nye County

facts.fact: The 24-mile unpaved byway crosses a volcanic field of cinder cones and basalt flows; Lunar Crater has been a National Natural Landmark since 1973.
The loop leaves US 6 about mile marker 79 east of Tonopah, and Easy Chair Crater is one of the first craters seen.

byways.name: Mt. Wilson Back Country Byway
byways.where: Around the Wilson Creek Range near Pioche, Lincoln County

facts.fact: The gravel byway circles the Wilson Creek Range through an old volcanic caldera grown over with pinyon and juniper, with aspen and ponderosa pine higher up.
Along the way are historic cabins, a pioneer cemetery and the mining town of Pioche.

byways.review: BLM's own text gives both 66 and 64 miles; catalog maps 88.

byways.name: Red Rock Canyon Back Country Byway
byways.where: 13-mile one-way Scenic Loop, Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area, Clark County

facts.fact: The byway is a 13-mile paved loop through Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area with several pullouts.
Timed entry reservations are required from October 1 to May 31, 8 am to 5 pm.

byways.review: Distinct from the state byway on SR 159 (Red Rock Road).

byways.name: Barrel Springs Back Country Byway
byways.where: Surprise Valley/Barrel Springs loop from Cedarville, California, into Washoe County, Nevada

facts.fact: The Surprise Valley Barrel Springs Back Country Byway is a 93-mile loop that begins and ends in Cedarville, California, and includes stretches in Nevada on improved gravel and dirt.
Pronghorn, bighorn sheep and sage-grouse live along the route, and willets use the spring lakes.

byways.review: Managed by BLM California (Applegate Field Office); url is the BLM guidebook download page.

byways.name: Buckhorn Back Country Byway
byways.where: California and Washoe County, Nevada
byways.review: Managed from California; no BLM page fetched and no facts gathered. Leave to the California chapter.

byways.name: The Loneliest Road in America
byways.designation: Nickname of US 50 across Nevada, adopted by the state as a promotional name
byways.where: US 50 from Lake Tahoe across central Nevada to the Utah line

facts.fact: Life magazine called US 50 across Nevada 'The Loneliest Road in America' in July 1986, meaning it as a slight, and state officials adopted the name as a slogan.
The highway crosses wide desert valleys separated by mountain ranges, using 17 passes in Nevada.

byways.review: Not on NDOT's scenic byway list. Two NDOT byways overlap it: Lake Tahoe East Shore and US Highways 6/50/93.

byways.name: Extraterrestrial Highway
byways.where: SR 375 from US 93 at Crystal Springs to US 6 at Warm Springs, Lincoln and Nye counties

facts.fact: SR 375 runs 98 miles past the edge of the Nellis range near Area 51; reports of UFO sightings led the state to name it the Extraterrestrial Highway in 1996.
Rachel, near the midpoint, serves tourists and UFO seekers with alien-themed businesses.

byways.review: Not on NDOT's scenic byway list.

issues: NDOT's byway page and map PDF return HTTP 403 to non-browser user agents (Cloudflare-style block). They were read with a plain browser user agent string carrying no personal data; the Rambleroo UA is refused.

Counts disagree: the NDOT web page says 1 All-American Road, 3 National Scenic Byways and 14 Nevada Scenic Byways (18); the 2023 map PDF says 13 Nevada byways and lists 17 numbered entries (Las Vegas north and south as one). This chapter lists 18, splitting the Las Vegas entry as the web page does.

The National Scenic Byway Foundation lists two state byways absent from NDOT's 2023 map: Nevada Way in Boulder City (5.8 mi) and the Washoe Valley route on US 395 Alternate (30 mi). It omits Baker Road, Lehman Caves Road and Mt Rose Highway. These look like NSBF data errors or un-designated proposals, but NDOT should confirm.
Hoover Dam Road (SR 172) is on the 2023 map but not on the 2015 list; its designation date is unknown.

Catalog duplicates: kyle-canyon-road-state-route-157-71118 and deer-creek-road-state-route-158-71119 are parts of mt-charleston-scenic-byway-39806 and should not be drawn as separate members. Catalog 2457 covers three state byways (Pyramid Lake, Sutcliffe-Nixon, Gerlach) and 2456 covers parts of two (Lake Tahoe North Shore and East Shore); several members share a bywayId.
Catalog 2456 (28 mi, Stateline to Incline Village) may not include SR 28 west of Incline Village to Crystal Bay or US 50 east of Spooner Summit toward Carson City, both part of the state byways.
Catalog red-rock-canyon-road-2035 maps 20 miles against 8.8 designated miles of SR 159; check that it does not trace the BLM Scenic Loop (catalog 68961).
Catalog labels the-loneliest-road-in-america-2033 and extraterrestrial-highway-2029 'Nevada State Scenic Byway', but neither is on NDOT's list; they are listed separately as named highways.
US Highways 6/50/93 (63 mi) has no catalog line and cannot be selected from the NDOT route layer by attribute; it needs a clipped geometry.
No agency page found for Mt Rose Highway, Lamoille Canyon Road (old USFS recarea URL now redirects), Great Basin Highway or US 6/50/93; url null.

BLM Nevada's byway page links each byway to recreation.gov 'gateways' pages that return 404; the BLM Nevada byways page is used as url instead. BLM mileages disagree with the catalog for Bitter Springs (28 vs 24), Mt. Wilson (64/66 vs 88) and Gold Butte (62 vs 56).
Buckhorn Back Country Byway was not researched (managed by BLM California); no blurb.
